extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and editors of observational epidemiology research (epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing complete, transparent reports of observational epidemiologic studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), including use of the STROBE checklist and relevant extensions/translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE checklist (items to include in reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: A checklist of items that should be included in articles reporting observational research (designed for cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STROBE checklist files are available (combined and separated by study design) in Word/PDF; an Explanation and Elaboration paper describing items and examples is also available. Use the checklist to guide what to report in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete transparency: planned, done, found, interpreted
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers need to know what was planned (and what was not), what was done, what was found, and what the results mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main aim of STROBE is to reduce incomplete and inadequate reporting so readers can assess strengths and weaknesses. Reporting should clearly state pre-specified plans vs deviations, detailed methods and results, and interpretation of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply checklist to the whole report
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE applies to the whole report (not just selected sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist covers items across the full manuscript (title/abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, other information). Ensure each relevant item for the chosen study design is addressed somewhere in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the checklist appropriate to study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the STROBE checklist variant that matches the study design: cohort, case-control, or cross-sectional (or the combined checklist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are separate downloadable checklists for cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies. Use the version tailored to the design being reported; extensions exist for other specific designs/areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE is guidance, not design/conduct prescription
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendations are guidance on how to report observational research well and are not prescriptions for designing or conducting studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not interpret the checklist as methodological requirements for study conduct; rather, it specifies what to report about what was planned and performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist is not a quality assessment instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: The STROBE checklist is not an instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the checklist as a scoring tool to judge methodological quality; its purpose is to improve completeness and transparency of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use extensions for specialised topics and designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, use STROBE extensions tailored to specific topics or designs (examples include STREGA for genetic association studies, STROBE-ME for molecular epidemiology, STROME-ID for infectious disease molecular epidemiology, STROBE-MR for Mendelian randomization, RECORD for routinely-collected health data, STROBE-nut for nutritional epidemiology, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The STROBE initiative supports and lists many extensions; choose the extension most relevant to the topic/design to ensure domain-specific reporting items are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference abstract reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a STROBE checklist draft of items to be included when reporting observational studies in conference abstracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the abstract-specific checklist when preparing conference abstracts to ensure essential items are communicated in limited space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of translations and fillable checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE materials (statement, explanation and checklists) have been translated into multiple languages and online fillable checklists are available (e.g., via GoodReports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult available translations for non-English reporting and consider using online fillable checklists to facilitate completion and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination and copyright for extensions/translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The STROBE authors request that anyone intending to use STROBE for further extensions, translations or other related work contact the coordinating group first; the original STROBE articles are copyrighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the STROBE coordinating group to coordinate efforts, avoid duplication, and obtain permission for re-publication of STROBE material in other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living initiative: revisions encouraged based on critique and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE is an ongoing process with future revisions of recommendations based on comments, critique and new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users are encouraged to provide feedback; guideline developers expect to update the statement and produce further extensions as needed.
